description: Oracle Database 23ai health metric catalog. Derived from dbi services scoring framework v0.30+.
release_notes:
v1.11.0 (2026-10-08): Absolute target. Data Guard primary fix: on a primary the collector omits the standby open mode and the Data Guard statistics are empty, while dataguard_configured is true, so a healthy primary read three missing critical checks (100 dropped to 84). BAK-4.5 standby_health now also needs its own value, and the Data Guard statistics checks PERF-4.1 dataguard_apply_lag, PERF-4.2 dataguard_transport_lag, PERF-4.3 dataguard_archive_gap, PERF-4.4 dataguard_protection_mode and PERF-4.6 dataguard_apply_rate (the collector counts local apply processes, none on a primary, so it read false on every healthy primary) apply on a standby (its open mode was reported), so a failed statistics query on a real standby still reads as missing. From package 1.17.0 an uncollected check counts 0 points, so the checks the collector omits because they do not apply apply only when their value is present: BAK-5.2 fra_usage_pct (no recovery area), CAP-4.3 archive_log_volume_daily (NOARCHIVELOG), CAP-4.2 sequence_cache_size (no busy sequence), PERF-1.9 sga_target and PERF-1.10 pga_aggregate_target (the other memory management mode), and the parameters absent on some versions: PERF-2.11 adaptive_plans, PERF-2.13 cursor_sharing_exact, SEC-3.7 audit_sys_operations, SEC-3.8 audit_trail_destination, FUT-2.5 control_mgmt_pack_access, FUT-2.6 securefiles_adoption. Until the collector tells "does not apply" from "could not collect", a collection failure on these reads as not applicable. v1.10.0 (2026-09-28): The five declarations (rpo_target, rto_target, security_posture, growth_headroom_target, dr_topology) carry the new declared_target flag, echoed by the engine in context.declarations. BAK-4.4 dataguard_configured now counts on every Enterprise Edition estate and is not required when dr_topology=none is declared (optional_when), instead of being judged only under a declared Data Guard topology; undeclared estates are required to have it. The rest of the Oracle counterpart of the PostgreSQL 1.13.0 target model is planned for the next release.
v1.9.0 (2026-09-03): Oracle Technology Leader review (2026-08-27). Retired BAK-1.3 archive_lag (wrong on non-Data-Guard databases where DEST_ID 1 has a NULL status), BAK-1.4 archive_multiplexing (duplicate of BAK-1.7, kept critical), PERF-1.1 buffer_cache_hit_ratio (a ratio of 100 percent says nothing about health), CAP-1.10 tablespace_fragmentation (meaningless with autoextend) and CAP-3.8 system_stats_gathered (current practice is not to gather; replaced by CAP-3.11 system_stats_at_defaults). CAP-1.2 asm_diskgroup_usage promoted to critical, guarded on its own presence so estates without ASM are not capped. BAK-1.5 redo_log_size threshold corrected to 512 MB (the collector emits megabytes; the previous bytes bound failed every instance). PERF-1.4 becomes ASMM-only. SEC-3.8 applies only under traditional auditing. BAK-2.6 and SEC-1.7 become attestations. PERF-1.11 prefers PGA_AGGREGATE_LIMIT (new capture PERF-1.13). First technical_anchor (the SQL behind the metric) and rationale fields, mostly the reviewer's own queries. Maturity: measurement-reviewed (2026-09-23). v1.6.0 (2026-07-01): Manual-metric gaps reported by the collector. Removed duplicate PERF-1.7 memory_config_pct_of_ram, which double-counted instance-memory-vs-RAM with the v1.10.0 engine-derived PERF-1.11 oracle_memory_pct_of_ram in perf_cache (the richer derived range metric is retained; no rule referenced PERF-1.7). Re-tagged autoupgrade_readiness (FUT-3.7) and config_backup_exists (FUT-4.5) sources ['sql']->['manual'] — operational attestations that are not SQL-queryable, so they previously read not-provided and never surfaced in the manual UI. Added offsite_backup (BAK-5.4, important, backup_retention) and dr_plan_documented (BAK-4.10, advisory, backup_recovery) to reach PostgreSQL manual-set parity; dr_plan_documented is distinct from dataguard_configured. 160 -> 161 metrics; subcategory budgets unchanged (fixed maxPoints). Engine unchanged (1.10.0). Thresholds/weights TL to refine. v1.5.0 (2026-06-21): PG-parity maturity + license/pack model. Migrated 10 coarse edition gates to precise license_requirement (diagnostic_pack/tuning_pack/enterprise_edition). Added 47 metrics (113 -> 160) across all 5 pillars: license-expressible coverage (partitioning/RAC/ADG/ACO/ASO), MAA backup/DG (redo redundancy, standby redo logs, RMAN catalog, ADG real-time apply, FSFO), CIS security hardening (listener, profiles, network ACLs, SYS audit, audit destination), capacity (SYSAUX/undo headroom/PDB resource plan & count/datafile policy/partitioning), performance (instance-memory-vs-RAM derived, SQL plan baselines, adaptive plans, single-block I/O latency, RAC GC latency/services), and future-proofing (mgmt-pack-access, SecureFiles, hidden-params, AutoUpgrade, DST). Added 4 cross-metric rules (TDE keystore backup, HugePages, PDB density, SYSAUX purge) -> 13. weight:0.5 de-pad on genuine always-pass captures (top_wait_events + sga/pga capture). undo_retention now profile-keyed. Engine 1.10.0 adds the oracle_memory_pct_of_ram derived formula. Thresholds calibrated from CIS Oracle Benchmark + Oracle MAA/docs (TL to refine).
v1.7.0: Coherence expansion. Closed the RTO hole — OR-CR-RTO-1/2 link rto_target to recovery evidence (Data Guard; recovery_tested). Attestation corroboration: OR-CR-ATT-1 (recovery_tested vs last_rman_backup_age), OR-CR-ATT-2 (tablespace_encryption vs tde_encrypted_tablespaces). New declared-target metrics: security_posture (SEC-4.9), growth_headroom_target (CAP-4.9), dr_topology (PERF-4.7), each wired to coherence rules (SECPOST-1/2, CAP-1, DR-1/2). OR-CR-FUT-1 links upgrade_plan to latest_patch. 10 new rules (13->23), 3 new metrics (161->164). Declaration is never graded: every target enum is all-pass; penalties come only from coherence rules. Capacity link uses tablespace_usage count semantic (gt 0), and SECPOST-1 gates on edition=enterprise so Standard Edition is never penalised for TDE it cannot license.
v1.7.1 (2026-07-21): Prose-only proofreading pass over display names, descriptions, remediations and consistency-rule texts for the TL review (typos, unclear phrasing, command casing; stale 100MB redo value aligned to 512MB threshold in BAK-1.5 remediation; SEC-2.1 remediation now uses ADMINISTER KEY MANAGEMENT syntax). No threshold, weight, gate, or structural change. v1.8.0 (2026-07-22): Target-aware + gate-escalation cycle (package 1.14.0). Fixed CAP-4.8 undo_tablespace_headroom, whose max_pct_of storage_size_kb made it unable to ever fail, to a plain max 85 percent. Retired PERF-2.6 adaptive_cursor_sharing, a duplicate of PERF-2.13 cursor_sharing_exact (now 163 metrics). Added license_requirement advanced_security to SEC-2.1 and SEC-2.4 so SE2 estates are not penalised for TDE they cannot license; gated BAK-4.4 dataguard_configured on enterprise_edition and applies_when dr_topology in [dg_async, dg_sync, rac_dg] so an SE or DR-none estate is not taxed for Data Guard. Seeded declaration-keyed thresholds (evaluation_config.by_declaration): CAP-1.2 asm_diskgroup_usage tightens with a tighter growth_headroom_target; PERF-4.1/4.2 Data Guard lag relax to the declared rpo_target, with undeclared estates keeping the 30s/60s absolutes. Added OR-CR-RPO-1 porting the PostgreSQL RPO-coherence rule (aggressive rpo_target with daily/no RMAN and no standby zeroes rpo_target and caps backup_recovery at 60 percent). FUT-3.1 upgrade_plan all-pass conversion deferred to a later Oracle pass, since it needs a compensating no-plan-while-behind rule.

metrics.description: Whether the database runs in ARCHIVELOG mode. Required for redo log archiving and point-in-time recovery.
metrics.remediation: Enable ARCHIVELOG mode: SHUTDOWN IMMEDIATE; STARTUP MOUNT; ALTER DATABASE ARCHIVELOG; ALTER DATABASE OPEN;

technical_anchor.summary: Reads the archiving mode of the database from V$DATABASE.
technical_anchor.query: SELECT LOG_MODE FROM V$DATABASE

metrics.description: Whether at least one LOG_ARCHIVE_DEST is defined and enabled. Without one, archiving has nowhere to write.
metrics.remediation: Configure LOG_ARCHIVE_DEST_1 to a valid path or Data Guard standby

technical_anchor.summary: Counts valid archive destinations in V$ARCHIVE_DEST; without the TARGET filter the query also works on a standby.
technical_anchor.query: SELECT COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM V$ARCHIVE_DEST WHERE STATUS = 'VALID'

metrics.description: Smallest online redo log group in megabytes. Undersized logs (below 512 MB) cause excessive log switches and checkpoint pressure under real workloads. The collector emits megabytes (MIN(BYTES)/1024/1024).
metrics.remediation: Resize redo log groups to at least 512MB using ALTER DATABASE DROP/ADD LOGFILE GROUP

technical_anchor.summary: Reads the smallest redo log group size from V$LOG, in megabytes.
technical_anchor.query: SELECT MIN(BYTES)/1024/1024 AS min_size_mb FROM V$LOG

metrics.rationale: Oracle Technology Leader review (2026-08-27): the previous bound of 536870912 was in bytes while the collector emits megabytes, so every instance failed the metric.

metrics.description: Average redo log switches per hour (V$LOG_HISTORY, last 24h). More than ~4-6/h means undersized logs or redo storms — checkpoint pressure and archive churn follow.
metrics.remediation: Resize online redo logs toward a 15-20 minute switch cadence at peak.

metrics.description: Whether a regular RMAN backup schedule (daily or more frequent) exists. Required for predictable RPO.
metrics.remediation: Configure an RMAN backup script and schedule it with Oracle Scheduler or cron

technical_anchor.summary: Counts database and archivelog backups over the last eight days in V$RMAN_BACKUP_JOB_DETAILS to corroborate the declared schedule.
technical_anchor.query:
select DB_INCR+DB_FULL DB_BACKUPS,ARCHIVELOGS ARCHIVELOG_BACKUPS from
(select count(*) DB_INCR from V$RMAN_BACKUP_JOB_DETAILS where START_TIME > sysdate - 8 and INPUT_TYPE = 'DB INCR') DB_INCR,
(select count(*) DB_FULL from V$RMAN_BACKUP_JOB_DETAILS where START_TIME > sysdate - 8 and INPUT_TYPE = 'DB FULL') DB_FULL,
(select count(*) ARCHIVELOGS from V$RMAN_BACKUP_JOB_DETAILS where START_TIME > sysdate - 8 and INPUT_TYPE = 'ARCHIVELOG') ARCHIVELOGS;

metrics.description: Age of the last successful RMAN backup. Backups older than 24h widen the recovery point window.
metrics.remediation: Check V$RMAN_BACKUP_JOB_DETAILS for recent failures and investigate RMAN log

technical_anchor.summary: Reads the age in hours of the last completed RMAN backup from V$RMAN_BACKUP_JOB_DETAILS.
technical_anchor.query: SELECT ROUND((CAST(SYSTIMESTAMP AS DATE) - MAX(END_TIME)) * 24, 1) AS age_hours FROM V$RMAN_BACKUP_JOB_DETAILS WHERE STATUS LIKE 'COMPLETED%'

metrics.description: Whether RMAN VALIDATE or CROSSCHECK runs regularly. Unverified backups may be unrestorable when needed.
metrics.remediation: Schedule a regular RMAN validation of the database and its archivelogs: BACKUP VALIDATE CHECK LOGICAL DATABASE ARCHIVELOG ALL;

technical_anchor.summary: Manual attestation; the validation run that backs it.
technical_anchor.query: RMAN> BACKUP VALIDATE CHECK LOGICAL DATABASE ARCHIVELOG ALL;

metrics.description: Whether Data Pump logical exports run on a schedule. A complement for smaller databases: it gives selective, object-level recovery beyond physical RMAN backups, at a cost that does not scale to large databases.
metrics.remediation: Configure regular Data Pump exports for logical backup capability

metrics.description: Whether RMAN has explicit settings (retention, autobackup, optimization). All-defaults usually means RMAN was never deliberately set up.
metrics.remediation: Configure RMAN: CONFIGURE RETENTION POLICY, CONFIGURE BACKUP OPTIMIZATION ON, CONFIGURE CONTROLFILE AUTOBACKUP ON

technical_anchor.query: SELECT COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM V$RMAN_CONFIGURATION

metrics.description: Whether RMAN backup compression is on. Reduces storage footprint and (often) backup window.
metrics.remediation: Enable RMAN compression: CONFIGURE COMPRESSION ALGORITHM 'BASIC'; BASIC is included in the database license, while LOW, MEDIUM and HIGH require the Advanced Compression option. Compression trades backup time and CPU on the database server for storage.
metrics.rationale: Oracle Technology Leader review (2026-08-27): compression may lengthen the backup window and load the server; only BASIC is free of the Advanced Compression license.

technical_anchor.query: SELECT COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM V$RMAN_CONFIGURATION WHERE NAME LIKE '%COMPRESSION%' AND VALUE != 'CLEAR'

metrics.description: Whether Oracle Flashback Database is on. Enables rapid PITR without restoring from backup, and in Data Guard environments lets a former primary be reinstated as a standby after a failover instead of being rebuilt.
metrics.remediation: Enable Flashback: ALTER DATABASE FLASHBACK ON; (requires FRA and ARCHIVELOG mode)

technical_anchor.query: SELECT FLASHBACK_ON FROM V$DATABASE

metrics.description: Whether RMAN automatically backs up the control file (CONFIGURE CONTROLFILE AUTOBACKUP). Without it, recovery after control file loss is far harder.
metrics.remediation: Enable RMAN: CONFIGURE CONTROLFILE AUTOBACKUP ON;

technical_anchor.query: SELECT VALUE FROM V$RMAN_CONFIGURATION WHERE NAME = 'CONTROLFILE AUTOBACKUP'

metrics.description: V$BLOCK_CHANGE_TRACKING status. With BCT, level-1 incrementals read only changed blocks; without it they scan the full database. EE feature.
metrics.remediation: ALTER DATABASE ENABLE BLOCK CHANGE TRACKING (EE; negligible overhead).

technical_anchor.query: SELECT STATUS FROM V$BLOCK_CHANGE_TRACKING

metrics.description: Whether a Recovery Point Objective is documented for this database. Without one, backup frequency is not anchored to a business need.
metrics.remediation: Define and document RPO target based on business requirements

metrics.description: Whether a Recovery Time Objective is documented for this database. Without one, restore design is not anchored to a business need.
metrics.remediation: Define and document RTO target based on business requirements

metrics.description: Whether the RMAN restore procedure has been exercised in the last 90 days. Untested restores can fail silently for months.
metrics.remediation: Schedule regular RMAN restore tests to a non-production environment; as a minimum, run a simulated restore regularly: RMAN> RESTORE DATABASE VALIDATE;

technical_anchor.summary: Manual attestation; the minimum simulated restore that backs it.
technical_anchor.query: RMAN> RESTORE DATABASE VALIDATE;

metrics.description: Whether an Oracle Data Guard standby exists. Provides HA/DR beyond what offline backups offer.
metrics.remediation: Configure Oracle Data Guard for high availability and disaster recovery

technical_anchor.query: SELECT COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM V$ARCHIVE_DEST WHERE TARGET = 'STANDBY' AND STATUS = 'VALID'

metrics.description: State of the Data Guard standby. A standby that is not mounted or open, or whose apply process (MRP) is not running, cannot fulfill its DR role. The apply check counts V$MANAGED_STANDBY processes in APPLYING_LOG or WAIT_FOR_LOG.
metrics.remediation: Check V$DATABASE and Data Guard broker status; investigate apply lag and errors

technical_anchor.summary: On the standby, counts running apply processes in V$MANAGED_STANDBY; must be greater than 0.
technical_anchor.query: select count(*) from v$managed_standby where status in ('APPLYING_LOG','WAIT_FOR_LOG');

metrics.description: Whether the database enforces logging of all changes (V$DATABASE.FORCE_LOGGING). Required for standby integrity and complete recoverability; NOLOGGING writes are unrecoverable from redo.
metrics.remediation: ALTER DATABASE FORCE LOGGING (after assessing bulk-load windows).

technical_anchor.query: select force_logging from v$database;

metrics.description: DG_BROKER_START. Broker-managed configurations get validated switchovers, observer/FSFO support, and drift checks; manual Data Guard is where failovers go wrong. Collector omits this metric when no Data Guard is configured.
metrics.remediation: Enable the broker (DGMGRL) and register the configuration.

technical_anchor.summary: Reads the DG_BROKER_START parameter; TRUE means the broker manages the configuration.
technical_anchor.query: select value from v$parameter where name='dg_broker_start';

metrics.description: Whether RMAN has an explicit retention policy. Default retention may not match business compliance windows.
metrics.remediation: Configure RMAN: CONFIGURE RETENTION POLICY TO RECOVERY WINDOW OF 7 DAYS; (or redundancy)

technical_anchor.query: SELECT VALUE FROM V$RMAN_CONFIGURATION WHERE NAME = 'RETENTION POLICY'

metrics.description: Fast Recovery Area utilization measured on usable space: used minus reclaimable, over the size limit. Above 80% risks archive write failure and database hangs. Reclaimable space is not a problem; it is freed automatically.
metrics.remediation: Increase DB_RECOVERY_FILE_DEST_SIZE or purge obsolete backups with RMAN DELETE OBSOLETE

technical_anchor.summary: Computes FRA usage from V$RECOVERY_FILE_DEST after subtracting reclaimable space.
technical_anchor.query:
SELECT
  ROUND(SPACE_LIMIT / 1073741824, 2) AS fra_size_gb,
  ROUND((SPACE_USED - SPACE_RECLAIMABLE) / 1073741824, 2) AS fra_used_gb,
  ROUND((SPACE_USED - SPACE_RECLAIMABLE) * 100.0 / NULLIF(SPACE_LIMIT, 0), 1) AS fra_pct_used
FROM V$RECOVERY_FILE_DEST

metrics.description: Whether archive log retention spans the RMAN recovery window. Premature deletion breaks PITR for older restore points.
metrics.remediation: Ensure archive log destination has sufficient space and DELETE INPUT is not configured too aggressively

technical_anchor.query: SELECT VALUE FROM V$RMAN_CONFIGURATION WHERE NAME = 'ARCHIVELOG DELETION POLICY'

metrics.description: Whether a copy of RMAN backups (or Data Pump exports) is kept at a second location — a different building, region, or cloud object store (3-2-1 rule). Single-site backups share fate with the primary during site-level incidents.
metrics.remediation: Replicate RMAN backups to a second site or cloud object store (e.g., OCI Object Storage / S3); confirm the offsite copy is independently restorable.

metrics.description: Whether Oracle Net (SQLNET) encryption is REQUIRED for client connections. REQUESTED still allows cleartext when the client refuses; only REQUIRED guarantees encrypted traffic.
metrics.remediation: Set SQLNET.ENCRYPTION_SERVER=REQUIRED (or move endpoints to TCPS/TLS).

technical_anchor.summary: Counts session banners of the current session that carry AES native encryption; more than 0 means the connection is encrypted.
technical_anchor.query: SELECT count(*) FROM V$SESSION_CONNECT_INFO WHERE SID = SYS_CONTEXT('USERENV','SID') and instr(NETWORK_SERVICE_BANNER,'AES') > 0;

metrics.description: Whether every profile assigned to a non-locked user has a password verification function, not only the DEFAULT profile. Without one, users can set weak, short or reused passwords.
metrics.remediation: Assign ORA12C_STRONG_VERIFY_FUNCTION (or custom) to all profiles via ALTER PROFILE

technical_anchor.summary: Reads the verify function per profile from DBA_PROFILES; the DEFAULT profile is the common case, but users may sit on other profiles.
technical_anchor.query: SELECT PROFILE, LIMIT FROM DBA_PROFILES WHERE RESOURCE_NAME = 'PASSWORD_VERIFY_FUNCTION';

metrics.description: Profile FAILED_LOGIN_ATTEMPTS limit. High/unlimited values let brute-force attempts continue indefinitely.
metrics.remediation: ALTER PROFILE DEFAULT LIMIT FAILED_LOGIN_ATTEMPTS 5;

metrics.description: Profile PASSWORD_LIFE_TIME setting. Long-lived passwords increase exposure when credentials leak.
metrics.remediation: ALTER PROFILE DEFAULT LIMIT PASSWORD_LIFE_TIME 90;

metrics.description: Oracle accounts using default or well-known passwords, excluding accounts that are EXPIRED and LOCKED. SYS and SYSTEM are included. Each open account with a default password is a free path in for attackers.
metrics.remediation: Change default passwords for all Oracle internal accounts (SYS, SYSTEM, DBSNMP, etc.)

technical_anchor.summary: Counts accounts with a default password that are still usable (not EXPIRED & LOCKED); SYS and SYSTEM are included.
technical_anchor.query: SELECT COUNT(*) AS defpwd_count FROM DBA_USERS_WITH_DEFPWD d JOIN DBA_USERS u ON u.USERNAME = d.USERNAME WHERE u.ACCOUNT_STATUS NOT LIKE 'EXPIRED & LOCKED%'

metrics.description: Whether Transparent Data Encryption protects sensitive tablespaces or the whole CDB. Required for at-rest data confidentiality.
metrics.remediation: Configure TDE: ADMINISTER KEY MANAGEMENT SET KEY IDENTIFIED BY ... WITH BACKUP; ALTER TABLESPACE ... ENCRYPTION ONLINE ENCRYPT;

technical_anchor.query: SELECT COUNT(*) AS enc_count FROM V$ENCRYPTED_TABLESPACES

metrics.description: Status of the Oracle Wallet/HSM. A closed keystore blocks TDE operations and queries on encrypted data. Conditional critical: applies_when gates it on TDE actually being in use (tde_encrypted_tablespaces >= 1); on non-TDE estates it is not applicable. Rule OR-CR-TDE-1 is a findings-only annotation so the critical is carried once. Collectors must emit V$ENCRYPTION_WALLET.STATUS as the raw string (not a boolean).
metrics.remediation: Open wallet: ADMINISTER KEY MANAGEMENT SET KEYSTORE OPEN IDENTIFIED BY ...;

technical_anchor.query: SELECT STATUS FROM V$ENCRYPTION_WALLET WHERE ROWNUM = 1

metrics.description: Whether SQLNET data integrity checksums are in use, observed from the session banner (Crypto-checksumming). Without them, in-flight tampering goes undetected. This check covers native network encryption; TLS endpoints carry their own integrity and are assessed differently.
metrics.remediation: Set SQLNET.CRYPTO_CHECKSUM_SERVER = REQUIRED in sqlnet.ora

technical_anchor.summary: Counts session banners of the current session that mention Crypto-checksumming; 0 means no integrity check.
technical_anchor.query:
select count(*)
from v$session_connect_info
where SID = sys_context('USERENV','SID') and instr(NETWORK_SERVICE_BANNER,'Crypto-checksumming') > 1

metrics.description: Whether tablespaces holding sensitive data are TDE-encrypted — an attestation that the data classification maps onto the encrypted set, not just that one encrypted tablespace exists (SEC-2.1).
metrics.remediation: Encrypt sensitive tablespaces: ALTER TABLESPACE ... ENCRYPTION ONLINE ENCRYPT;

metrics.description: DB_BLOCK_CHECKSUM mode. Required (TYPICAL or FULL) to detect physical block corruption before it propagates.
metrics.remediation: ALTER SYSTEM SET DB_BLOCK_CHECKSUM = TYPICAL;

technical_anchor.query: SELECT VALUE FROM V$PARAMETER WHERE NAME = 'db_block_checksum'

metrics.description: Whether Oracle uses Unified Auditing (vs traditional/mixed mode). Required for a consolidated, tamper-resistant audit trail.
metrics.remediation: Relink Oracle binary with unified auditing enabled and restart instance

technical_anchor.query: SELECT VALUE FROM V$OPTION WHERE PARAMETER = 'Unified Auditing'

metrics.description: Whether at least one unified audit policy is enabled. Without one, auditing is on in name only.
metrics.remediation: Create and enable an audit policy: CREATE AUDIT POLICY ...; AUDIT POLICY ...;

technical_anchor.query: SELECT COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM AUDIT_UNIFIED_ENABLED_POLICIES

metrics.description: Whether Fine-Grained Auditing (FGA) covers sensitive table/column access. Useful for compliance with data-access regulations. EE-only (DBMS_FGA); applies_when gates it on edition=enterprise.
metrics.remediation: Use DBMS_FGA.ADD_POLICY for column-level auditing on sensitive data

technical_anchor.query: SELECT COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM DBA_AUDIT_POLICIES

metrics.description: Whether the unified audit trail lives in a dedicated, write-protected location. Otherwise audit records can be altered or purged.
metrics.remediation: Configure audit trail to OS or DB with restricted access; consider syslog forwarding

metrics.description: Whether system privilege usage (especially DBA/SYSDBA) is captured in audit. Required for accountability of high-privilege actions.
metrics.remediation: Enable auditing of CREATE SESSION WITH SYSDBA, DBA role usage, and privilege escalation

technical_anchor.query: SELECT COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM AUDIT_UNIFIED_POLICIES p WHERE (p.AUDIT_OPTION LIKE '%LOGON%' OR p.AUDIT_OPTION LIKE '%CREATE%SESSION%') AND p.POLICY_NAME IN (SELECT POLICY_NAME FROM AUDIT_UNIFIED_ENABLED_POLICIES)

metrics.description: Whether DBMS_AUDIT_MGMT purge/archive jobs manage the unified audit trail. Unmanaged, AUDSYS grows until SYSAUX fills — an outage caused by the audit system itself.
metrics.remediation: Configure DBMS_AUDIT_MGMT.CREATE_PURGE_JOB with an archive-then-purge policy.

technical_anchor.summary: Counts enabled audit-trail cleanup jobs in DBA_AUDIT_MGMT_CLEANUP_JOBS.
technical_anchor.query: select count(*) from DBA_AUDIT_MGMT_CLEANUP_JOBS where job_status='ENABLED';

metrics.description: Number of grantees of the DBA role. Each extra grant widens the blast radius of a compromised account.
metrics.remediation: Revoke DBA role from application and generic accounts; use least-privilege roles

technical_anchor.query:
SELECT COUNT(*) AS dba_count
FROM DBA_ROLE_PRIVS
WHERE GRANTED_ROLE = 'DBA'
  AND GRANTEE NOT IN ('SYS', 'SYSTEM')

metrics.description: Application users with ANY% system privileges (e.g. SELECT ANY TABLE). These privileges bypass object-level access control.
metrics.remediation: Revoke ANY% privileges from application accounts; grant specific object privileges instead

technical_anchor.query: SELECT COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM DBA_SYS_PRIVS WHERE PRIVILEGE LIKE '%ANY%' AND GRANTEE NOT IN ('SYS','SYSTEM','DBA','DATAPUMP_IMP_FULL_DATABASE')

metrics.description: PUBLIC execute grants on sensitive packages (UTL_FILE, UTL_TCP, DBMS_JAVA). These enable file/network access for any logged-in user.
metrics.remediation: Revoke EXECUTE on dangerous packages from PUBLIC; grant only to required roles

technical_anchor.query: SELECT COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM DBA_TAB_PRIVS WHERE GRANTEE = 'PUBLIC' AND PRIVILEGE = 'EXECUTE' AND TABLE_NAME IN ('UTL_FILE','UTL_TCP','UTL_HTTP','UTL_SMTP','DBMS_JAVA','DBMS_LOB')

metrics.description: REMOTE_LOGIN_PASSWORDFILE mode. SHARED password files allow SYS access from any database sharing the file.
metrics.remediation: Set REMOTE_LOGIN_PASSWORDFILE=EXCLUSIVE to prevent shared password file attacks

technical_anchor.query: SELECT VALUE FROM V$PARAMETER WHERE NAME = 'remote_login_passwordfile'

metrics.description: OS_AUTHENT_PREFIX setting. An empty prefix lets OS users connect without an Oracle prefix marker, weakening account hygiene.
metrics.remediation: Review OS-authenticated accounts; consider disabling OS_AUTHENT_PREFIX if not needed

technical_anchor.query: SELECT VALUE FROM V$PARAMETER WHERE NAME = 'os_authent_prefix'

metrics.description: O7_DICTIONARY_ACCESSIBILITY must be FALSE so ANY privileges do not reach SYS-owned dictionary objects.
metrics.remediation: ALTER SYSTEM SET O7_DICTIONARY_ACCESSIBILITY=FALSE SCOPE=SPFILE; restart.

metrics.description: Count of tablespaces above the critical fill threshold (95%), measured against the maximum autoextended size of their files rather than the current allocation. Any tablespace at that level risks ORA-1653 unable-to-extend write failures.
metrics.remediation: Extend datafiles or add files to the affected tablespaces; enable AUTOEXTEND with MAXSIZE as a safety net.

metrics.description: ASM diskgroup utilization. Above 80% reduces rebalance headroom, risks running out of space mid-allocation, and degrades disk I/O times. Counts only when the collector reports a diskgroup value, so estates without ASM are not capped for a missing critical. Target-aware (v1.8.0): a tighter declared growth_headroom_target lowers the ceiling.
metrics.remediation: Add disks to ASM diskgroup: ALTER DISKGROUP ... ADD DISK ...;
metrics.rationale: Oracle Technology Leader review (2026-08-27): critical because I/O times suffer when a diskgroup is too full. Guarded on the metric's own presence rather than a storage-type fact: a missing fact evaluates false and would silently drop the metric.

technical_anchor.query: SELECT NAME, ROUND((TOTAL_MB - FREE_MB)/TOTAL_MB * 100) AS pct FROM V$ASM_DISKGROUP

metrics.description: Temporary tablespace utilization. Above 90% causes ORA-1652 errors during sorts, hashes, and global temporary tables.
metrics.remediation: Add temp files: ALTER TABLESPACE TEMP ADD TEMPFILE ... SIZE ...;

technical_anchor.summary: Computes temp tablespace usage against the maximum autoextended size of the tempfiles (DBA_TEMP_FILES, DBA_TEMP_FREE_SPACE).
technical_anchor.query:
SELECT tbs."Name",
       tbs."Nb tempfile(s)",
       decode(tbs2.contents,'TEMPORARY','TEMP','UNDO','UNDO','PERMANENT','DATA') "Type",
       decode(tbs2.extent_management,'LOCAL','LM-','DICTONARY','DM-') || substr(tbs2.allocation_type,1,3) "Extent Mgmt",
       tbs2.segment_space_management "Segment Mgmt",
       round(tbs."Size MB"/1024,2) "Allocated Size GB",
       round(fs.FREE_SPACE/1024/1024/1024,2) "Free Space GB",
       round(tbs."Max Size MB"/1024,2) "Max Size GB",
       round((((tbs."Size MB" - (fs.FREE_SPACE/1024/1024)) * 100) / tbs."Max Size MB"),2) "Percent used",
       tbs2.block_size/1024 || ' KB' "Block size",
       decode(tbs2.logging,'LOGGING','YES','NO') "Logging"
FROM (
SELECT t.tbs "Name", count(*) "Nb tempfile(s)", sum(t.filesize)/1024/1024 "Size MB", sum(t.rmax)/1024/1024 "Max Size MB"
FROM
  ( SELECT tbs.tablespace_name tbs,
           df.file_id,
           CASE
               WHEN df.bmaxsize - df.bsize < df.bnext THEN df.bsize*tbs.block_size
               ELSE df.bmaxsize*tbs.block_size
           END rmax,
           df.bsize*tbs.block_size filesize
   FROM
     (SELECT tablespace_name, file_id, blocks bsize, CASE WHEN autoextensible = 'YES' THEN maxblocks ELSE blocks END bmaxsize, CASE WHEN autoextensible = 'YES' THEN increment_by ELSE 0 END bnext
      FROM dba_temp_files) df,
     (SELECT tablespace_name,
             block_size
      FROM dba_tablespaces) tbs
   WHERE tbs.tablespace_name = df.tablespace_name ) t
GROUP BY t.tbs
ORDER BY 1 desc) tbs,
dba_tablespaces tbs2,
dba_temp_free_space fs
WHERE tbs."Name"=tbs2.tablespace_name
and tbs."Name"=fs.tablespace_name;

metrics.description: Whether critical datafiles have AUTOEXTEND on. Acts as a safety net when fixed-size files near their limit.
metrics.remediation: Enable autoextend: ALTER DATABASE DATAFILE '...' AUTOEXTEND ON NEXT 256M MAXSIZE UNLIMITED;

technical_anchor.summary: Counts datafiles without autoextend, excluding the undo tablespace (fixed-size undo is the recommended setup).
technical_anchor.query: SELECT COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM DBA_DATA_FILES WHERE AUTOEXTENSIBLE = 'NO' and tablespace_name not in (select value from v$parameter where name='undo_tablespace');

metrics.description: Whether segment growth (Segment Advisor or DBA_SEGMENTS) is reviewed regularly. Required to anticipate capacity needs.
metrics.remediation: Schedule Segment Advisor job and review DBA_SEGMENTS growth regularly

metrics.description: Count of PDBs not in their expected open mode plus unresolved entries in PDB_PLUG_IN_VIOLATIONS. A PDB stuck in MOUNTED or RESTRICTED is an outage users see. applies_when gates it on a multitenant (CDB) architecture; non-CDB instances report it not applicable.
metrics.remediation: Open the PDB, resolve plug-in violations, and persist state (ALTER PLUGGABLE DATABASE ... SAVE STATE).

technical_anchor.summary: Adds PDBs not open read-write (or restricted) to unresolved plug-in violations.
technical_anchor.query:
select incorrectly_opened+plug_in_violations
from
(select count(*) incorrectly_opened from v$pdbs where (open_mode <> 'READ WRITE' or restricted='YES') and name <> 'PDB$SEED'),
(select count(*) plug_in_violations from pdb_plug_in_violations where status <> 'RESOLVED');

metrics.description: Session-slot consumption against the SESSIONS limit. Above 80% risks ORA-00018 'maximum number of sessions exceeded'.
metrics.remediation: Increase SESSIONS/PROCESSES parameters or implement connection pooling

technical_anchor.query:
SELECT
  (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM V$SESSION WHERE TYPE = 'USER') AS current_sessions,
  (SELECT VALUE FROM V$PARAMETER WHERE NAME = 'sessions')  AS max_sessions

metrics.description: Process-slot consumption against the PROCESSES limit. Above 80% risks ORA-00020 'maximum number of processes exceeded'.
metrics.remediation: ALTER SYSTEM SET PROCESSES=... SCOPE=SPFILE; and restart, or implement DRCP

technical_anchor.summary: Computes process slots in use against the PROCESSES parameter.
technical_anchor.query:
SELECT (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM V$PROCESS) AS current_procs,
       (SELECT VALUE FROM V$PARAMETER WHERE NAME = 'processes') AS max_procs
FROM DUAL

metrics.description: Whether DRCP or application-level connection pooling is in place. Required to support many short-lived clients without exhausting PROCESSES.
metrics.remediation: Configure DRCP: EXECUTE DBMS_CONNECTION_POOL.START_POOL(); or use application connection pool

technical_anchor.query: SELECT COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM DBA_CPOOL_INFO WHERE STATUS = 'ACTIVE'

metrics.description: Tables/indexes with stale optimizer statistics. Stale stats lead the optimizer to pick poor execution plans.
metrics.remediation: Run DBMS_STATS.GATHER_DATABASE_STATS or enable auto stats collection

technical_anchor.summary: Counts stale object statistics outside Oracle-maintained schemas.
technical_anchor.query: SELECT COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM DBA_TAB_STATISTICS WHERE STALE_STATS = 'YES' AND OWNER NOT IN (SELECT USERNAME FROM DBA_USERS WHERE ORACLE_MAINTAINED='Y');

metrics.description: Whether the Oracle automatic optimizer statistics collection task is enabled. Without it, stats drift quickly under heavy DML.
metrics.remediation: Enable auto stats: EXECUTE DBMS_AUTO_TASK_ADMIN.ENABLE(client_name => 'auto optimizer stats collection', ...);

technical_anchor.query: SELECT COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM DBA_AUTOTASK_CLIENT WHERE CLIENT_NAME = 'auto optimizer stats collection' AND STATUS = 'ENABLED'

metrics.description: Outstanding Segment Advisor shrink/reclaim recommendations. Untouched recommendations let storage stay fragmented.
metrics.remediation: Run ALTER TABLE ... SHRINK SPACE for heavily fragmented segments

technical_anchor.query: SELECT COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM DBA_ADVISOR_FINDINGS WHERE TASK_NAME LIKE '%Segment%' AND TYPE = 'PROBLEM'

metrics.description: UNDO_RETENTION setting. Too short causes ORA-1555 'snapshot too old' on long queries and limits Flashback Query.
metrics.remediation: ALTER SYSTEM SET UNDO_RETENTION = 900; then size for the longest-running query: MAXQUERYLEN from V$UNDOSTAT times the average undo blocks per second gives the minimum undo tablespace size for that query.

technical_anchor.summary: Reads the longest query duration seen by the undo statistics, the input for undo sizing.
technical_anchor.query: SELECT MAX(MAXQUERYLEN) FROM V$UNDOSTAT;

metrics.description: Object count in the Oracle recyclebin. Excessive accumulation consumes tablespace storage and slows DDL queries.
metrics.remediation: PURGE DBA_RECYCLEBIN; to reclaim space from dropped objects

technical_anchor.query: SELECT COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM DBA_RECYCLEBIN

metrics.description: Invalid PL/SQL objects (procedures, packages, triggers) in production schemas. A handful of stale objects is noise; sustained counts are runtime errors waiting to happen.
metrics.remediation: Recompile with utlrp.sql or ALTER ... COMPILE; investigate objects that stay invalid.

technical_anchor.summary: Counts invalid objects outside Oracle-maintained schemas.
technical_anchor.query: SELECT COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM DBA_OBJECTS WHERE STATUS = 'INVALID' AND OWNER NOT IN (select username from dba_users where oracle_maintained='Y');

metrics.description: Undo tablespace utilization. Above 80% risks shortened retention, ORA-1555 errors, and DML failures.
metrics.remediation: Increase the undo tablespace size or reduce UNDO_RETENTION. Prefer a fixed-size undo tablespace without autoextend, sized for the retention and the longest queries.

technical_anchor.summary: Computes undo tablespace usage from the active undo extents and the undo datafiles.
technical_anchor.query:
SELECT ROUND(NVL(
  (SELECT SUM(e.BYTES) FROM DBA_UNDO_EXTENTS e WHERE e.STATUS IN ('ACTIVE','UNEXPIRED')) * 100
  / NULLIF((SELECT SUM(f.BYTES) FROM DBA_DATA_FILES f WHERE f.TABLESPACE_NAME IN
             (SELECT TABLESPACE_NAME FROM DBA_TABLESPACES WHERE CONTENTS = 'UNDO')), 0)
, 0), 1) AS pct FROM DUAL

metrics.description: CACHE value on high-use sequences. Small caches (below 20) cause SQ enqueue contention under concurrent inserts. The collector selects sequences by a LAST_NUMBER heuristic to skip rarely used ones; a sequence that starts high is missed.
metrics.remediation: ALTER SEQUENCE ... CACHE 100; for sequences used in high-frequency inserts

metrics.description: Whether daily archive log generation is monitored against storage projections. Surprise growth can fill the FRA and stop archiving. The volume to keep depends on the RMAN archivelog deletion policy and the interval between archivelog backups.
metrics.remediation: Review V$ARCHIVED_LOG for daily volume trends and size FRA accordingly

technical_anchor.query: SELECT ROUND(NVL(SUM(BLOCKS * BLOCK_SIZE) / 1048576, 0)) AS mb_24h FROM V$ARCHIVED_LOG WHERE COMPLETION_TIME > SYSDATE - 1

metrics.description: Whether an Oracle Database Resource Manager plan is active. Without one, runaway sessions can monopolize CPU/IO. EE-only (DBRM); applies_when gates it on edition=enterprise. Collector caveat: a default maintenance plan should not read as 'active'.
metrics.remediation: Enable Resource Manager: ALTER SYSTEM SET RESOURCE_MANAGER_PLAN = 'DEFAULT_PLAN';

technical_anchor.query: SELECT VALUE FROM V$PARAMETER WHERE NAME = 'resource_manager_plan'

metrics.description: Library cache hit ratio (shared SQL/PL/SQL reuse). Below 99% suggests too many hard parses and shared-pool churn.
metrics.remediation: Increase SHARED_POOL_SIZE or SGA_TARGET; review hard parse rate

technical_anchor.query:
SELECT
  ROUND((SUM(PINS) - SUM(RELOADS)) * 100.0 / NULLIF(SUM(PINS), 0), 1) AS lib_cache_hit_pct
FROM V$LIBRARYCACHE

metrics.description: Whether PGA_AGGREGATE_TARGET or PGA_AGGREGATE_LIMIT is set explicitly. Without bounds, runaway sort/hash workareas can starve the host.
metrics.remediation: Set PGA_AGGREGATE_TARGET based on available memory and workload type

technical_anchor.query: SELECT VALUE FROM V$PARAMETER WHERE NAME = 'pga_aggregate_target'

metrics.description: Whether Automatic Shared Memory Management is in use: MEMORY_TARGET is 0 and SGA_TARGET is greater than 0. Automatic Memory Management (MEMORY_TARGET) fails the check; manual sizing of every SGA pool is brittle as workloads shift.
metrics.remediation: Use ASMM, not AMM: set MEMORY_TARGET = 0 and SGA_TARGET > 0 (with PGA_AGGREGATE_TARGET sized separately).

technical_anchor.summary: Reads MEMORY_TARGET and SGA_TARGET; ASMM means memory_target 0 and sga_target above 0.
technical_anchor.query: select name, value FROM V$PARAMETER WHERE NAME in ('memory_target', 'sga_target');

metrics.rationale: Oracle Technology Leader review (2026-08-27): do not use AMM, always ASMM.

metrics.description: RESULT_CACHE_MODE setting. MANUAL or FORCE makes the result cache available for repeated lookup queries.
metrics.remediation: Consider using RESULT CACHE hint or RESULT_CACHE_MODE=FORCE for stable lookup queries

technical_anchor.query: SELECT VALUE FROM V$PARAMETER WHERE NAME = 'result_cache_mode'

metrics.description: Whether AWR is active with a reasonable snapshot interval. Without it, no historical performance baseline exists for diagnosis. Requires Diagnostics Pack (EE); applies_when gates it on edition=enterprise so SE2 estates (statspack) are not penalised for a pack they cannot license.
metrics.remediation: EE + Diagnostics Pack: ensure AWR snapshots run (default). SE2: deploy statspack and document the baseline practice.

technical_anchor.summary: Reads the management pack access parameter; DIAGNOSTIC or DIAGNOSTIC+TUNING is the prerequisite for AWR use.
technical_anchor.query: SELECT VALUE FROM V$PARAMETER WHERE NAME = 'control_management_pack_access';

metrics.description: Whether SQL Plan Management (SPM) or SQL profiles pin plans for critical queries. Without them, optimizer changes can regress performance silently. EE-only (SQL Plan Management); applies_when gates it on edition=enterprise.
metrics.remediation: Use DBMS_SPM to capture and evolve SQL plan baselines for critical queries

technical_anchor.query: SELECT COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM DBA_SQL_PLAN_BASELINES WHERE ENABLED = 'YES'

metrics.description: Top-SQL average elapsed time, judged against the declared workload. OLTP statements above 30s are pathological; OLAP batch queries legitimately run minutes.
metrics.remediation: Review AWR Top SQL report; tune high-elapsed queries using DBMS_SQLTUNE or SQL Tuning Advisor

technical_anchor.query: SELECT ROUND(NVL(MAX(ELAPSED_TIME / NULLIF(EXECUTIONS, 0)) / 1000000, 0), 1) AS max_avg_s FROM V$SQL WHERE EXECUTIONS > 0 AND PARSING_SCHEMA_NAME NOT IN ('SYS','SYSTEM')

metrics.description: Hard parse ratio against total parse calls, judged against the declared workload. OLTP above 2% indicates literal SQL or cursor leaks; ad-hoc analytic sessions parse by nature.
metrics.remediation: Use bind variables; increase CURSOR_SHARING or OPEN_CURSORS; review application code

technical_anchor.summary: Computes the hard-parse share of all parses from V$SYSSTAT.
technical_anchor.query:
SELECT ROUND(
  (SELECT VALUE FROM V$SYSSTAT WHERE NAME = 'parse count (hard)') /
  NULLIF((SELECT VALUE FROM V$SYSSTAT WHERE NAME = 'parse count (total)'), 0) * 100
) AS hard_parse_pct FROM DUAL

metrics.description: Whether the Automatic SQL Tuning Advisor job runs and its findings are reviewed. Useful for catching tuning opportunities before users complain. EE-only (Tuning Pack); applies_when gates it on edition=enterprise.
metrics.remediation: Enable AUTO_SQLTUNE task; review DBA_SQLTUNE_FINDINGS regularly

technical_anchor.query: SELECT COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM DBA_AUTOTASK_CLIENT WHERE CLIENT_NAME = 'sql tuning advisor' AND STATUS = 'ENABLED'

metrics.description: OPTIMIZER_MODE setting. ALL_ROWS is the supported cost-based default; legacy modes (RULE, FIRST_ROWS_n) are discouraged.
metrics.remediation: Set OPTIMIZER_MODE=ALL_ROWS; avoid RULE mode (desupported)

technical_anchor.query: SELECT VALUE FROM V$PARAMETER WHERE NAME = 'optimizer_mode'

metrics.description: Share of total wait time spent on enqueue (lock) waits. Above 1% suggests blocking sessions or hot rows.
metrics.remediation: Investigate V$ENQUEUE_STAT and V$SESSION for blocking sessions; review application locking

technical_anchor.query: SELECT ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN EVENT LIKE 'enq%' THEN TIME_WAITED_MICRO ELSE 0 END) / NULLIF(SUM(TIME_WAITED_MICRO),0) * 100) AS pct FROM V$SYSTEM_EVENT WHERE WAIT_CLASS != 'Idle'

metrics.description: ORA-00060 deadlocks recorded in the alert log over the last 24h. Each deadlock kills a transaction and points to bad lock ordering.
metrics.remediation: Review deadlock trace files in $ADR_HOME; fix application lock ordering

metrics.description: Rate of TX (row lock) contention waits. Sustained contention indicates hot rows, long-running DML, or missing indexes on FK columns.
metrics.remediation: Use SELECT FOR UPDATE NOWAIT or SKIP LOCKED; review COMMIT frequency

technical_anchor.query: SELECT TIME_WAITED FROM V$SYSTEM_EVENT WHERE EVENT = 'enq: TX - row lock contention'

metrics.description: Library cache latch miss ratio against gets. Above 1% suggests excessive hard parsing or shared-pool fragmentation.
metrics.remediation: Reduce hard parses; increase SHARED_POOL_SIZE; use bind variables

technical_anchor.query: SELECT ROUND(MISSES / NULLIF(GETS, 0) * 100, 2) AS miss_pct FROM V$LATCH WHERE NAME = 'library cache'

metrics.description: Data Guard standby apply lag. Sustained lag widens RPO and can violate protection-mode commitments. applies_when gates it on dataguard_configured; collectors must emit the lag as numeric seconds (not a V$DATAGUARD_STATS interval string).
metrics.remediation: Investigate V$DATAGUARD_STATS; check redo apply parallelism on standby

technical_anchor.summary: On the standby, reads the apply lag from V$DATAGUARD_STATS (interval string, converted to seconds by the collector).
technical_anchor.query: SELECT VALUE FROM V$DATAGUARD_STATS WHERE NAME = 'apply lag'

metrics.description: Data Guard transport lag: redo not yet received by the standby. Network or LGWR/ARCH issues widen RPO during a failover. Collected on the standby (V$DATAGUARD_STATS is only populated there). applies_when gates it on dataguard_configured; the by_declaration band relaxes the bound to the declared RPO.
metrics.remediation: Review network bandwidth between primary and standby; check LGWR/ARCH processes

technical_anchor.summary: On the standby, reads the transport lag from V$DATAGUARD_STATS (interval string, converted to seconds by the collector).
technical_anchor.query: SELECT VALUE FROM V$DATAGUARD_STATS WHERE NAME = 'transport lag'

metrics.description: Archive log gaps between primary and standby. Any gap means standby is missing redo and cannot complete recovery on failover. applies_when gates it on dataguard_configured.
metrics.remediation: Use RMAN to restore missing archive logs; check V$ARCHIVE_GAP on primary

technical_anchor.query: SELECT COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM V$ARCHIVE_GAP

metrics.description: Data Guard protection mode. Choice trades RPO vs availability — should be set deliberately, not left at default. applies_when gates it on dataguard_configured so standalone primaries (which always report MAXIMUM PERFORMANCE) drop the metric instead of trivially passing.
metrics.remediation: Set the protection mode through the broker, not with SQL: DGMGRL> EDIT CONFIGURATION SET PROTECTION MODE AS MAXAVAILABILITY;

technical_anchor.query: SELECT PROTECTION_MODE FROM V$DATABASE

metrics.description: Major Oracle version in use (parsed numerically from the version string). Versions below 19c are out of error correction; 19c itself requires Extended Support — see MOS 742060.1 for the current schedule.
metrics.remediation: Plan the upgrade to a supported long-term release (19c minimum, 23ai target); verify Extended Support coverage for 19c estates.

technical_anchor.query: SELECT VERSION_FULL FROM V$INSTANCE

metrics.description: Months since the most recent Release Update was applied (DBA_REGISTRY_SQLPATCH). Beyond 12 months, known CVEs remain unpatched.
metrics.remediation: Apply the latest quarterly RU; align with the organizational patch window.

technical_anchor.query:
SELECT ACTION, TARGET_VERSION, DESCRIPTION
FROM DBA_REGISTRY_SQLPATCH
ORDER BY ACTION_TIME DESC
FETCH FIRST 3 ROWS ONLY

metrics.description: Time remaining before Extended Support ends. Less than 12 months requires an active upgrade plan.
metrics.remediation: Review My Oracle Support Lifetime Support Policy and plan upgrade before extended support ends

metrics.description: Whether the applied-patch inventory is documented and tracked. Required for vulnerability response and change management.
metrics.remediation: Maintain patch inventory using opatch lspatches output in change management system

metrics.description: Whether Real Application Clusters (RAC) or Data Guard is deployed. Required for instance- or site-level high availability. RAC/DG are EE-only; applies_when gates it on edition=enterprise. SE2 DR posture is still scored via the BAK-4.x Data Guard metrics.
metrics.remediation: Deploy Oracle RAC for instance-level HA or Data Guard for site-level DR

technical_anchor.query: SELECT VALUE FROM V$PARAMETER WHERE NAME = 'cluster_database'

metrics.description: Whether database storage runs on Oracle ASM. Preferred over raw/filesystem for rebalance, mirroring, and RAC support.
metrics.remediation: Consider migrating to ASM for improved storage management and RAC support

technical_anchor.query: SELECT NAME, ROUND((TOTAL_MB - FREE_MB)/TOTAL_MB * 100) AS pct FROM V$ASM_DISKGROUP

metrics.description: Whether the database uses SPFILE (not PFILE). SPFILE allows persistent ALTER SYSTEM SCOPE=SPFILE changes and is the supported default.
metrics.remediation: Create SPFILE from PFILE: CREATE SPFILE FROM PFILE; then restart

technical_anchor.query: SELECT VALUE FROM V$PARAMETER WHERE NAME = 'spfile'

metrics.description: Whether the instance is a CDB (V$DATABASE.CDB). Non-CDB has been desupported since 21c — every 19c non-CDB must convert during its next upgrade. On 23ai this is always true.
metrics.remediation: Plan the non-CDB to PDB conversion as part of the 19c-to-23ai upgrade path.

metrics.description: Whether a documented Oracle version upgrade plan is on file. Required to avoid scrambling when support ends.
metrics.remediation: Create an upgrade roadmap and test using Oracle AutoUpgrade tool

metrics.description: Deprecated Oracle features still active. Each one is a forced rework before the next major upgrade.
metrics.remediation: Query V$OPTION_USAGE and review MOS Doc 2337415.1 for deprecated feature list

technical_anchor.query:
SELECT NAME, VALUE
FROM V$PARAMETER
WHERE ISDEPRECATED = 'TRUE'
  AND VALUE IS NOT NULL
  AND VALUE != '0'
  AND VALUE != 'FALSE'
  AND VALUE != ''

metrics.description: Whether key initialization parameters align with Oracle best-practice recommendations. Drift here often hides slow-burn performance issues.
metrics.remediation: Review Oracle configuration best practices; use ORAchk for automated parameter checks

technical_anchor.summary: Reads the four parameters the best-practice check compares with their recommended values.
technical_anchor.query:
SELECT NAME, VALUE FROM V$PARAMETER
WHERE NAME IN ('db_block_size', 'open_cursors', 'session_cached_cursors', 'optimizer_adaptive_plans')

metrics.description: Recency of the last ORAchk health check. Older than 90 days means findings may be stale and patches may be missed.
metrics.remediation: Download ORAchk from My Oracle Support and run regularly

metrics.description: Alignment between COMPATIBLE and the running Oracle version. Lagging COMPATIBLE blocks new features and is a common upgrade oversight.
metrics.remediation: After confirming no rollback needed, update COMPATIBLE to match actual version

technical_anchor.query: SELECT VALUE FROM V$PARAMETER WHERE NAME = 'compatible'

metrics.description: Whether the Oracle Enterprise Manager agent is installed and the target is being managed. Useful for centralized monitoring and lifecycle ops.
metrics.remediation: Deploy Oracle EM agent for centralized monitoring and lifecycle management

metrics.description: Whether alert-log monitoring and notifications are wired up (OEM, Zabbix, or similar). Without alerting, problems surface only when users complain.
metrics.remediation: Configure alert log monitoring and critical threshold alerts (tablespace, process limits)

metrics.description: AWR snapshot retention period. Below 30 days makes it hard to baseline the workload and diagnose intermittent issues. Diagnostics Pack (EE); applies_when gates it on edition=enterprise.
metrics.remediation: EXECUTE DBMS_WORKLOAD_REPOSITORY.MODIFY_SNAPSHOT_SETTINGS(retention => 43200);

technical_anchor.summary: Reads the AWR retention from DBA_HIST_WR_CONTROL.
technical_anchor.query: SELECT MAX(EXTRACT(DAY FROM RETENTION)) FROM DBA_HIST_WR_CONTROL

metrics.description: Whether architecture diagrams and operational runbooks are documented and current. Stale docs slow incident response.
metrics.remediation: Maintain up-to-date architecture diagrams, runbooks, and change log

metrics.description: Status of the most recent RMAN backup within the last 24h. Failed/aborted backups put recovery at risk.
metrics.remediation: Investigate RMAN backup failures in V$RMAN_BACKUP_JOB_DETAILS

technical_anchor.summary: Reads the status and type of the most recent RMAN job from V$RMAN_BACKUP_JOB_DETAILS.
technical_anchor.query:
SELECT STATUS, START_TIME, INPUT_TYPE
  FROM V$RMAN_BACKUP_JOB_DETAILS
 WHERE START_TIME > SYSDATE - 1
 ORDER BY START_TIME DESC
 FETCH FIRST 1 ROWS ONLY

metrics.description: Whether profiles beyond DEFAULT exist. Custom profiles let app, service, and admin accounts have distinct password policies.
metrics.remediation: Create custom password profiles: CREATE PROFILE app_profile LIMIT ...

technical_anchor.query:
SELECT PROFILE, RESOURCE_NAME, LIMIT
FROM DBA_PROFILES
WHERE RESOURCE_TYPE = 'PASSWORD'
  AND PROFILE IN (
    SELECT PROFILE FROM DBA_USERS
    WHERE ACCOUNT_STATUS = 'OPEN'
      AND AUTHENTICATION_TYPE = 'PASSWORD'
  )
ORDER BY PROFILE, RESOURCE_NAME

metrics.description: Current active session count relative to CPU cores (the AAS-vs-cores yardstick): sustained activity beyond ~1.5x cores means queueing, session leaks, or runaway SQL. Falls back to an absolute cap of 200 when no system facts are declared.
metrics.remediation: Investigate high active session counts; check for session leaks or runaway queries

technical_anchor.summary: Active user sessions relative to CPU cores (V$OSSTAT NUM_CPU_CORES), the average-active-sessions yardstick.
technical_anchor.query:
SELECT (active_sessions/cpu_cores)*100 AS aas_vs_cores_percent, active_sessions FROM (select count(*) active_sessions from V$SESSION WHERE TYPE = 'USER' AND STATUS = 'ACTIVE'),
(select value cpu_cores from v$osstat where STAT_NAME='NUM_CPU_CORES');

metrics.description: Active undo size in MB. Excessive growth points to long-running transactions and risks blocking other DML.
metrics.remediation: Investigate long-running transactions causing undo growth

technical_anchor.query:
SELECT
  ROUND(SUM(BYTES) / 1048576, 0) AS undo_used_mb,
  STATUS
FROM DBA_UNDO_EXTENTS
GROUP BY STATUS
ORDER BY STATUS

metrics.description: Top non-idle wait events for the snapshot period. The shape of the wait profile drives most performance triage.
metrics.remediation: Review V$SYSTEM_EVENT for top wait events and tune accordingly

technical_anchor.query:
SELECT EVENT, TOTAL_WAITS, TIME_WAITED_MICRO / 1000000 AS time_waited_sec
FROM V$SYSTEM_EVENT
WHERE WAIT_CLASS != 'Idle'
ORDER BY TIME_WAITED_MICRO DESC
FETCH FIRST 5 ROWS ONLY

metrics.description: DBA_HIST_WR_CONTROL snapshot interval. Above 60 minutes, diagnosis loses resolution exactly when incidents need it. Diagnostics Pack (EE); applies_when gates it on edition=enterprise so SE2 reports it not applicable.
metrics.remediation: DBMS_WORKLOAD_REPOSITORY.MODIFY_SNAPSHOT_SETTINGS(interval => 30 or 60).

technical_anchor.query: SELECT MAX(EXTRACT(DAY FROM SNAP_INTERVAL)*1440 + EXTRACT(HOUR FROM SNAP_INTERVAL)*60 + EXTRACT(MINUTE FROM SNAP_INTERVAL)) FROM DBA_HIST_WR_CONTROL

metrics.description: Free memory in the shared pool. Meaningful for manually sized SGAs; under ASMM/AMM the pool resizes elastically and low free space is usually transient.
metrics.remediation: Increase SHARED_POOL_SIZE or SGA_TARGET to provide more shared pool memory

technical_anchor.query:
SELECT ROUND(BYTES / 1048576, 0) AS free_mb
FROM V$SGASTAT
WHERE POOL = 'shared pool' AND NAME = 'free memory'

metrics.description: USE_LARGE_PAGES on Linux. Multi-GB SGAs on 4 kB pages burn TLB entries and risk page-table bloat with many dedicated connections; the ONLY setting guarantees HugePages are used or the instance does not start. Incompatible with AMM (MEMORY_TARGET).
metrics.remediation: Configure vm.nr_hugepages for the SGA and set USE_LARGE_PAGES=ONLY; prefer SGA_TARGET/PGA_AGGREGATE_TARGET over MEMORY_TARGET.

metrics.description: Count of DBA_REGISTRY components not in VALID state. Anything else typically points to a half-applied patch or upgrade — it reflects patch-execution truth, so it lives beside the version/patch-level metrics (moved from future_foundation in v1.4.0).
metrics.remediation: Re-run the failed component installation or utlrp.sql; review DBA_REGISTRY history for the component.

technical_anchor.summary: Counts DBA_REGISTRY components that are neither VALID nor deliberately switched off.
technical_anchor.query: select count(*) from dba_registry where status <> 'VALID' and status <> 'OPTION OFF';

metrics.description: Whether every online redo log group has at least two members. A single-member group can lose the current redo on media failure, causing data loss. The check counts members per group; whether the members sit on separate storage is not verified. Two or three members per group is the ideal.
metrics.remediation: ALTER DATABASE ADD LOGFILE MEMBER so every group has 2 (ideally on separate disks or diskgroups) and at most 3 members.

technical_anchor.summary: Reads the smallest member count over all redo log groups from V$LOGFILE.
technical_anchor.query: SELECT MIN(cnt) FROM (SELECT GROUP#, COUNT(*) cnt FROM V$LOGFILE GROUP BY GROUP#)

metrics.rationale: Oracle Technology Leader review (2026-08-27): BAK-1.4 measured the same thing; one critical check kept.

metrics.description: Whether standby redo logs exist and are sized to the largest online redo log. Required for Data Guard real-time apply and low transport lag.
metrics.remediation: Create standby redo logs: (#online groups + 1) per thread, each sized to the largest online redo log.

technical_anchor.summary: Counts standby redo logs in V$STANDBY_LOG (Data Guard environments).
technical_anchor.query: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM V$STANDBY_LOG

metrics.description: Whether an RMAN recovery catalog is registered rather than relying on the controlfile alone. The catalog retains backup metadata beyond CONTROL_FILE_RECORD_KEEP_TIME and survives controlfile loss. Registration is only visible from the catalog database, so this is an attestation.
metrics.remediation: Create and register a recovery catalog (CREATE CATALOG; REGISTER DATABASE) and back it up.

technical_anchor.summary: Run against the recovery catalog database, not the target: the database must appear in RC_DATABASE.
technical_anchor.query: SELECT count(*) FROM rc_database WHERE name = '<db-name>';

metrics.description: Whether RMAN backupsets are written encrypted so off-host copies (tape/cloud/disk) are protected at rest. Transparent (TDE-based) mode requires Advanced Security.
metrics.remediation: CONFIGURE ENCRYPTION FOR DATABASE ON (transparent, needs ASO) or use SET ENCRYPTION (password-based).

technical_anchor.query: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM V$RMAN_CONFIGURATION WHERE UPPER(NAME) LIKE '%ENCRYPTION%'

metrics.description: Whether an RMAN ARCHIVELOG DELETION POLICY is configured so archived redo is reclaimed only after it is backed up (and applied to all standbys).
metrics.remediation: CONFIGURE ARCHIVELOG DELETION POLICY TO BACKED UP n TIMES TO DEVICE TYPE ... (APPLIED ON ALL STANDBY for DG).

technical_anchor.query: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM V$RMAN_CONFIGURATION WHERE UPPER(NAME) LIKE 'ARCHIVELOG DELETION POLICY%'

metrics.description: Whether the physical standby runs real-time apply while open read-only with apply (Active Data Guard). Real-time apply alone is not enough: the standby must also be open, or the license is not being used. Minimises apply lag / RPO and validates redo on the standby.
metrics.remediation: RECOVER MANAGED STANDBY DATABASE USING CURRENT LOGFILE; open read-only with ADG if licensed.

technical_anchor.summary: Counts destinations in real-time apply whose database mode is READ ONLY WITH APPLY.
technical_anchor.query: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM V$ARCHIVE_DEST_STATUS WHERE UPPER(RECOVERY_MODE) LIKE 'MANAGED%REAL TIME APPLY%' and DATABASE_MODE='READ ONLY WITH APPLY'

metrics.description: Whether Data Guard Fast-Start Failover is enabled so the broker fails over automatically within the configured lag limit, removing manual intervention from the RTO.
metrics.remediation: Enable Fast-Start Failover via the broker (ENABLE FAST_START FAILOVER) with an observer.

technical_anchor.query: SELECT FS_FAILOVER_STATUS FROM V$DATABASE

metrics.description: Whether a disaster recovery plan exists in writing — roles, RTO/RPO targets, and step-by-step restore/switchover runbooks. Distinct from having Data Guard deployed: a shop can run a standby-site or RMAN-restore DR strategy without Data Guard. Without a written plan, recovery decisions are improvised under stress.
metrics.remediation: Document the DR strategy: RTO/RPO objectives, standby/restore runbooks, contact roles, and a periodic review cadence.

metrics.description: Whether the TNS listener is hardened: ADMIN_RESTRICTIONS on, no external procedure (extproc) entry, secure registration, and logging enabled. An open listener allows remote reconfiguration and audit loss.
metrics.remediation: Set ADMIN_RESTRICTIONS_<listener>=ON, remove extproc, set SECURE_REGISTER_<listener>=TCPS/IPC, enable logging.

metrics.description: Whether user profiles cap resource usage (SESSIONS_PER_USER, IDLE_TIME, CPU) instead of UNLIMITED, limiting resource-exhaustion and abandoned-session exposure.
metrics.remediation: Set SESSIONS_PER_USER<=10 (CIS) and IDLE_TIME<=15 (STIG) on application profiles rather than UNLIMITED.

technical_anchor.query: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM DBA_PROFILES WHERE PROFILE='DEFAULT' AND RESOURCE_NAME IN ('SESSIONS_PER_USER','IDLE_TIME') AND LIMIT='UNLIMITED'

metrics.description: Whether profiles set INACTIVE_ACCOUNT_TIME so unused accounts are locked automatically, reducing dormant-credential risk.
metrics.remediation: ALTER PROFILE ... LIMIT INACTIVE_ACCOUNT_TIME 120 (or stricter) on application profiles.

technical_anchor.query: SELECT LIMIT FROM DBA_PROFILES WHERE PROFILE='DEFAULT' AND RESOURCE_NAME='INACTIVE_ACCOUNT_TIME'

metrics.description: Whether the TDE keystore/wallet is backed up separately from the encrypted database backup. RMAN does not back up the keystore; losing it makes encrypted backups unrecoverable.
metrics.remediation: Back up the keystore (ADMINISTER KEY MANAGEMENT BACKUP KEYSTORE). For a software wallet, locate it via V$ENCRYPTION_WALLET.WRL_PARAMETER and copy cwallet.sso and ewallet.p12 to a location distinct from the RMAN backups.

technical_anchor.summary: Manual attestation; the wallet location that must be backed up separately.
technical_anchor.query: SELECT WRL_PARAMETER FROM V$ENCRYPTION_WALLET;

metrics.description: Whether Oracle Data Redaction policies mask sensitive columns for non-privileged sessions. A defense-in-depth control requiring Advanced Security.
metrics.remediation: Define DBMS_REDACT.ADD_POLICY policies on identified sensitive columns.

technical_anchor.query: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM REDACTION_POLICIES

metrics.description: Whether TDE uses a strong algorithm (AES256) rather than a weaker/legacy cipher for encrypted tablespaces.
metrics.remediation: Rekey encrypted tablespaces to AES256 (ALTER TABLESPACE ... ENCRYPTION ... ENCRYPT with AES256).

technical_anchor.query: SELECT MIN(ENCRYPTIONALG) FROM V$ENCRYPTED_TABLESPACES

metrics.description: Whether privileged SYS/SYSDBA top-level actions are audited: AUDIT_SYS_OPERATIONS for traditional auditing, or a unified audit policy enabled for SYS under pure unified auditing (available from 19c, the default on 23ai).
metrics.remediation: Set AUDIT_SYS_OPERATIONS=TRUE under traditional auditing, or enable a unified audit policy for the SYS user (top-level actions, session evaluation) under pure unified auditing.

technical_anchor.summary: Under unified auditing, counts enabled policies that audit all top-level SYS actions.
technical_anchor.query: select count(*) from audit_unified_policies where policy_name in (select policy_name from audit_unified_enabled_policies where enabled_option='BY USER' and entity_name like '%SYS%' and entity_type='USER') and AUDIT_ONLY_TOPLEVEL='YES' and CONDITION_EVAL_OPT='SESSION' and AUDIT_OPTION='ALL';

metrics.description: Whether a traditional audit destination is active (AUDIT_TRAIL not NONE). Only meaningful under traditional auditing; with pure unified auditing the parameter is not consulted, so the metric does not apply.
metrics.remediation: Set AUDIT_TRAIL to DB,EXTENDED or OS, or migrate to unified auditing.

technical_anchor.summary: Reads the audit_trail parameter from V$PARAMETER.
technical_anchor.query: SELECT VALUE FROM V$PARAMETER WHERE NAME = 'audit_trail'

metrics.description: Whether outbound network ACLs (DBMS_NETWORK_ACL_ADMIN) are scoped to specific hosts/principals rather than wildcard-open, preventing arbitrary external connections from the database.
metrics.remediation: Replace wildcard ACLs with host/port- and principal-scoped APPEND_HOST_ACE grants.

technical_anchor.query: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM DBA_HOST_ACES WHERE HOST='*'

metrics.description: Whether the deprecated UTL_FILE_DIR parameter is unset (directory objects used instead). A populated UTL_FILE_DIR grants broad filesystem access.
metrics.remediation: Unset UTL_FILE_DIR and use DIRECTORY objects with explicit grants.

technical_anchor.summary: Reads the utl_file_dir parameter from V$PARAMETER.
technical_anchor.query: SELECT VALUE FROM V$PARAMETER WHERE NAME = 'utl_file_dir'

metrics.description: The declared security posture for this database (baseline, hardened, or regulated). Declaring it sets the expectation that configuration evidence — TDE, unified/traditional auditing — corroborates the claim; the declaration itself is never penalised.
metrics.remediation: Declare the security posture matching this database's compliance scope, then align TDE and auditing to it.

metrics.description: Whether SYSAUX usage is within bounds. Sustained growth past the default warn band usually signals AWR-retention or audit-occupant bloat; investigate before SYSAUX fills.
metrics.remediation: Review V$SYSAUX_OCCUPANTS; tune AWR retention / purge AUDSYS; resize SYSAUX.

technical_anchor.query: SELECT ROUND(used_percent) FROM DBA_TABLESPACE_USAGE_METRICS WHERE TABLESPACE_NAME='SYSAUX'

metrics.description: Whether autoextensible datafiles have a bounded MAXSIZE rather than UNLIMITED. UNLIMITED means the datafile ceiling: 32 GB for a smallfile and 32 TB for a bigfile tablespace at an 8 KB block size, so a runaway segment can consume the whole filesystem or diskgroup.
metrics.remediation: Set an explicit MAXSIZE on autoextensible datafiles and monitor headroom.

technical_anchor.summary: Counts autoextensible datafiles whose MAXBYTES is the UNLIMITED ceiling (32 GB smallfile or 32 TB bigfile at 8 KB blocks).
technical_anchor.query: SELECT COUNT(*) AS unbounded FROM DBA_DATA_FILES WHERE AUTOEXTENSIBLE = 'YES' AND MAXBYTES >= 34359721984

metrics.description: Whether large heap tables (segments above the partitioning threshold) are partitioned for manageability and pruning. Oracle considers tables above 2 GB partitioning candidates.
metrics.remediation: Partition large segments (range/list/hash) per the access pattern; requires the Partitioning option.

technical_anchor.query: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM DBA_SEGMENTS WHERE SEGMENT_TYPE='TABLE' AND BYTES > 2*1024*1024*1024 AND (OWNER, SEGMENT_NAME) NOT IN (SELECT OWNER, TABLE_NAME FROM DBA_PART_TABLES)

metrics.description: Whether peak open cursors per session stay below the OPEN_CURSORS limit. Hitting the limit raises ORA-1000 and aborts statements.
metrics.remediation: Raise OPEN_CURSORS to cover peak usage, or fix cursor leaks in the application.

technical_anchor.summary: Peak open cursors of any session as a share of OPEN_CURSORS, in the current container.
technical_anchor.query: SELECT ROUND(MAX(ss.value) / NULLIF((SELECT TO_NUMBER(value) FROM V$PARAMETER WHERE NAME='open_cursors'),0) * 100) FROM V$SESSTAT ss JOIN V$STATNAME sn ON ss.statistic#=sn.statistic# WHERE sn.name='opened cursors current' and ss.con_id=(sys_context('USERENV','CON_ID')) and ss.con_id=sn.con_id group by ss.con_id;

metrics.description: Whether the share of INACTIVE sessions is reasonable. The ratio matters at higher session counts: ten idle sessions are not a pooling problem, a thousand are. A high inactive ratio on a busy instance indicates pooling or leak issues consuming process slots.
metrics.remediation: Use connection pooling (DRCP), tune pool sizing, and close idle sessions / set IDLE_TIME.
metrics.rationale: Oracle Technology Leader review (2026-08-27): the ratio is only a signal together with the absolute session count.

technical_anchor.query: SELECT ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN status='INACTIVE' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)/NULLIF(COUNT(*),0)*100) FROM V$SESSION WHERE type='USER'

metrics.description: Whether fixed-object (X$/V$) statistics have been gathered. Missing fixed-object stats degrade dictionary/dynamic-view query plans.
metrics.remediation: Run DBMS_STATS.GATHER_FIXED_OBJECTS_STATS after major workload/version changes.

technical_anchor.query: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM DBA_TAB_STATISTICS WHERE OBJECT_TYPE='FIXED TABLE' AND LAST_ANALYZED IS NOT NULL

metrics.description: Whether DBMS_SCHEDULER jobs are completing. A backlog of FAILED runs means maintenance (stats, purges, backups driven by jobs) is silently not running.
metrics.remediation: Investigate DBA_SCHEDULER_JOB_RUN_DETAILS failures and fix the underlying jobs.

technical_anchor.query: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM DBA_SCHEDULER_JOB_RUN_DETAILS WHERE STATUS='FAILED' AND ACTUAL_START_DATE > SYSDATE-7

metrics.description: Whether global DBMS_STATS preferences (ESTIMATE_PERCENT auto, AUTO sampling, incremental stats for partitioned tables) follow current best practice rather than legacy overrides.
metrics.remediation: Review DBMS_STATS.GET_PREFS; restore AUTO_SAMPLE_SIZE / sensible global prefs.

technical_anchor.summary: Reads the global statistics preferences through DBMS_STATS.GET_PREFS.
technical_anchor.query: SELECT DBMS_STATS.GET_PREFS('ESTIMATE_PERCENT') FROM DUAL

metrics.description: Whether optimizer system statistics (SYS.AUX_STATS$) sit at the noworkload defaults. Current practice is to leave them there; gathered workload statistics that no longer match the hardware skew every cost estimate.
metrics.remediation: If workload system statistics were gathered and the hardware changed, delete them (DBMS_STATS.DELETE_SYSTEM_STATS) so the optimizer falls back to the noworkload defaults.

technical_anchor.summary: Counts the three noworkload default rows in SYS.AUX_STATS$; a count of 3 means the defaults are in place.
technical_anchor.query: select count(*) from sys.aux_stats$ where (PNAME='IOSEEKTIM' and PVAL1=10) or (PNAME='IOTFRSPEED' and PVAL1=4096) or (PNAME='CPUSPEEDNW' and pval1 is not null) and sname='SYSSTATS_MAIN' and PVAL1 is not null;

metrics.rationale: Oracle Technology Leader review (2026-08-27): gathering system statistics is no longer recommended; the replaced metric CAP-3.8 rewarded the opposite.

metrics.description: Whether a CDB resource plan allocates CPU/parallelism across PDBs. Without one, a noisy PDB can starve its siblings.
metrics.remediation: Create a CDB resource plan with shares/limits per PDB (DBMS_RESOURCE_MANAGER).

technical_anchor.query: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM V$RSRC_PLAN

metrics.description: Whether the user-PDB count is comfortably below MAX_PDBS. Approaching the limit blocks new PDB creation (ORA-65010).
metrics.remediation: Raise MAX_PDBS (within licensing) or consolidate/relocate PDBs before reaching the cap.

technical_anchor.summary: Compares the number of PDBs with the MAX_PDBS parameter.
technical_anchor.query: SELECT ROUND((SELECT COUNT(*) FROM V$PDBS WHERE CON_ID > 2) / NULLIF((SELECT TO_NUMBER(VALUE) FROM V$PARAMETER WHERE NAME='max_pdbs'),0) * 100) FROM DUAL

metrics.description: Whether non-expired undo stays below the allocated undo size. Once active+unexpired undo nears the allocation, the database steals unexpired extents and risks ORA-01555/ORA-30036.
metrics.remediation: Grow the undo tablespace or lower long-running DML pressure; size undo for the longest query + retention.

technical_anchor.query: SELECT ROUND(NVL((SELECT SUM(bytes) FROM dba_undo_extents WHERE status IN ('ACTIVE','UNEXPIRED')),0) / NULLIF((SELECT SUM(bytes) FROM dba_data_files df JOIN dba_tablespaces ts ON df.tablespace_name=ts.tablespace_name WHERE ts.contents='UNDO'),0) * 100) FROM dual

metrics.description: The planning horizon for which current tablespace headroom is expected to suffice (3, 6, or 12 months). Corroborated against observed tablespace utilisation; the declaration itself is never penalised.
metrics.remediation: Declare the growth horizon and ensure current tablespace utilisation leaves room to reach it before space is exhausted.

metrics.description: The configured SGA_TARGET. Captured to derive total instance memory vs host RAM; not scored on its own.
metrics.remediation: Informational capture; size SGA per workload and host RAM.

technical_anchor.query: SELECT VALUE FROM V$PARAMETER WHERE NAME = 'sga_target'

metrics.description: The configured PGA_AGGREGATE_TARGET. Captured to derive total instance memory vs host RAM; not scored on its own.
metrics.remediation: Informational capture; size PGA per workload and host RAM.

technical_anchor.query: SELECT VALUE FROM V$PARAMETER WHERE NAME = 'pga_aggregate_target'

metrics.description: Whether total instance memory (SGA_TARGET plus PGA_AGGREGATE_LIMIT when set, else PGA_AGGREGATE_TARGET) sits in a healthy band of physical RAM. Above ~80% starves the OS (swap risk); well below ~40% on a dedicated host wastes memory. On a host running several instances the sum across instances is what matters, which a single-database collection cannot see.
metrics.remediation: Right-size SGA+PGA to ~40-80% of RAM on a dedicated DB host (leave ~20% for the OS).
metrics.rationale: Oracle Technology Leader review (2026-08-27): take PGA_AGGREGATE_LIMIT instead of PGA_AGGREGATE_TARGET, and sum all instances on the server.

metrics.description: Whether PGA_AGGREGATE_LIMIT is set as a hard cap so runaway PGA cannot exhaust host memory (12c and later). When unset it defaults to twice PGA_AGGREGATE_TARGET.
metrics.remediation: Set PGA_AGGREGATE_LIMIT to a sane hard ceiling above PGA_AGGREGATE_TARGET.

technical_anchor.summary: Reads the pga_aggregate_limit parameter from V$PARAMETER.
technical_anchor.query: SELECT VALUE FROM V$PARAMETER WHERE NAME = 'pga_aggregate_limit'

metrics.description: The configured PGA_AGGREGATE_LIMIT in bytes. Captured to derive total instance memory vs host RAM; not scored on its own.
metrics.remediation: Informational capture; see PERF-1.12 for the hard-cap check.

technical_anchor.summary: Reads the PGA hard limit parameter.
technical_anchor.query: SELECT VALUE FROM V$PARAMETER WHERE NAME = 'pga_aggregate_limit'

metrics.rationale: Oracle Technology Leader review (2026-08-27): the PGA hard limit, not the target, is the real memory footprint; captured so PERF-1.11 can prefer it.

metrics.description: Whether SQL Plan Baselines protect critical statements from plan regressions. Deepens plan stability beyond capture-only.
metrics.remediation: Adopt SQL Plan Management for critical SQL; verify accepted/enabled baselines exist.

technical_anchor.query: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM DBA_SQL_PLAN_BASELINES WHERE ENABLED='YES' AND ACCEPTED='YES'

metrics.description: Whether OPTIMIZER_ADAPTIVE_PLANS is enabled (the 12.2+/19c default) so the optimizer corrects join-method mis-estimates at runtime.
metrics.remediation: Set OPTIMIZER_ADAPTIVE_PLANS=TRUE. OPTIMIZER_ADAPTIVE_STATISTICS is off by default; some workloads benefit from enabling it, so treat it as a per-estate choice.
metrics.rationale: Oracle Technology Leader review (2026-08-27): adaptive statistics may still be useful for some customers.

technical_anchor.summary: Reads the optimizer_adaptive_plans parameter from V$PARAMETER.
technical_anchor.query: SELECT VALUE FROM V$PARAMETER WHERE NAME = 'optimizer_adaptive_plans'

metrics.description: Whether average single-block read latency (db file sequential read) is within flash/SSD norms. High values point to storage I/O degradation inflating response time. Sourced from AWR.
metrics.remediation: Investigate storage/ASM; target <=1 ms on flash, <=5 ms on disk.

technical_anchor.query: SELECT ROUND(AVERAGE_WAIT*10, 2) FROM V$SYSTEM_EVENT WHERE EVENT='db file sequential read'

metrics.description: Whether CURSOR_SHARING is left at EXACT (recommended) rather than FORCE, which can cause bind-peeking and plan-stability problems.
metrics.remediation: Set CURSOR_SHARING=EXACT and fix non-bind SQL at the application instead.

technical_anchor.summary: Reads the cursor_sharing parameter from V$PARAMETER.
technical_anchor.query: SELECT VALUE FROM V$PARAMETER WHERE NAME = 'cursor_sharing'

metrics.description: Whether average RAC global-cache block receive latency is sub-millisecond. Higher values indicate interconnect or load problems degrading Cache Fusion.
metrics.remediation: Check the private interconnect (bandwidth, errors, jumbo frames) and instance load balancing.

technical_anchor.query: SELECT ROUND(AVG(AVERAGE_WAIT)*10, 2) FROM V$SYSTEM_EVENT WHERE EVENT LIKE 'gc %block%'

metrics.description: Whether application connections use named RAC services rather than the default DB service. Named services enable workload management, load balancing and Application Continuity.
metrics.remediation: Define and use application services (srvctl add service) instead of the default service.

technical_anchor.summary: Lists application services in the PDB, excluding the default and internal services.
technical_anchor.query: select name FROM DBA_SERVICES WHERE NAME NOT IN ('SYS$BACKGROUND','SYS$USERS') AND NAME NOT LIKE '%XDB' and name <> (select SYS_CONTEXT('USERENV', 'CON_NAME') from dual);

metrics.description: Whether the standby apply rate keeps pace with primary redo generation, so lag does not accumulate under load. Collected on the standby.
metrics.remediation: Tune apply (parallel recovery, real-time apply, I/O on the standby) so apply rate >= redo rate.

technical_anchor.summary: On the standby, reads the recovery progress rates; the average apply rate must keep up with the redo received.
technical_anchor.query: SELECT ITEM, SOFAR, UNITS FROM V$RECOVERY_PROGRESS WHERE ITEM IN ('Average Apply Rate', 'Active Apply Rate', 'Apply Time per Log')

metrics.description: The declared disaster-recovery topology (none, Data Guard async, Data Guard sync, or RAC + Data Guard). Corroborated against Data Guard configuration and protection mode; the declaration itself is never penalised.
metrics.remediation: Declare the DR topology in place and align Data Guard configuration / protection mode to it.

metrics.description: Whether the database DST/time-zone file is reasonably current. A stale file yields wrong TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE results and blocks cross-database transport.
metrics.remediation: Apply the latest DST patch and run the time-zone upgrade (DBMS_DST) during a window.

technical_anchor.query: SELECT TO_NUMBER(PROPERTY_VALUE) FROM DATABASE_PROPERTIES WHERE PROPERTY_NAME='DST_PRIMARY_TT_VERSION'

metrics.description: Whether CONTROL_MANAGEMENT_PACK_ACCESS matches the packs actually licensed. The EE default (DIAGNOSTIC+TUNING) silently enables licensable packs and creates audit exposure when they are unlicensed.
metrics.remediation: Set CONTROL_MANAGEMENT_PACK_ACCESS to match owned packs (NONE if Diagnostics/Tuning not licensed).

technical_anchor.summary: Reads the control_management_pack_access parameter from V$PARAMETER.
technical_anchor.query: SELECT VALUE FROM V$PARAMETER WHERE NAME = 'control_management_pack_access'

metrics.description: Whether LOBs use SecureFiles (the default, recommended store) rather than deprecated BasicFiles.
metrics.remediation: Set DB_SECUREFILE=PREFERRED/ALWAYS and migrate remaining BasicFiles LOBs online.

technical_anchor.summary: Reads the db_securefile parameter from V$PARAMETER.
